title: Krevia Phase 5.3 — Full Backend Regression and Background Worker Suspension Audit
objective: Complete the remaining verification after Krevia_Sprint_7.17_Phase5.2_Organization_Suspension_UAT: run the full backend regression suite, and audit every background worker in the codebase (not just the recruitment export worker) for organization-suspension awareness, fixing narrow, clearly-scoped gaps where found.
verdictRationale: The full canonical backend regression suite runs clean: the exact same 9 pre-existing, pre-Phase-5.1 failures appear before and after this task's changes (confirmed by running the suite twice — once before any Phase 5.3 worker fix, once after — and diffing the failure lists), and zero new failures were introduced. Four background workers with real, confirmed external side effects and no organization-suspension check were found and fixed with narrow, tested changes, closing the exact class of gap the task was scoped to find. One additional worker (the generic scheduled-job executor, which can send reminders and run AI agents with credit/token cost) was found to have the same gap but was deliberately NOT fixed in this pass — its dispatch pipeline spans several files and the correct policy for an already-queued scheduled job is a genuine product question, not a narrow, obviously-safe code change — so it is reported as an open blocker for an explicit decision, per the task's own instruction not to guess at an unclear policy.

Already uses --no-file-parallelism by design, consistent with the task's own instruction.

Two date-extraction assertions expect a date to resolve to 2026 but the LLM/orchestrator resolves it to 2027 — an LLM date-parsing behavior unrelated to authorization, workers, or anything touched by this task. Confirmed present in the baseline run.

partB_workerInventory.reasonNotFixed: This pipeline spans multiple files (SchedulerService -> JobDispatcher -> JobExecutor -> JobRegistry -> per-handler-type logic) and the correct policy is genuinely ambiguous in a way the four fixed workers were not: should an already-queued scheduled job for a now-suspended organization be silently skipped (risking a user-visible 'reminder never arrived' complaint once reactivated), deferred like resume parsing (risking an unbounded backlog of time-sensitive reminders that fire all at once on reactivation, some now stale/wrong), or terminally failed (losing it entirely)? None of these is obviously correct without a product/security decision, unlike the four fixed workers where 'do not take this specific action for a suspended org' was unambiguous. Per the task's own instruction to document rather than guess when the intended behavior isn't clear, this is reported as an open blocker, not silently fixed or silently ignored.

partB_workerInventory.worker: QueueConsumerWorker (the shared dispatcher for every QueueCategory, including RECRUITMENT_EXPORTS and NOTIFICATION_JOBS)
partB_workerInventory.queueOrTrigger: Self-ticking setInterval (2s), claims and dispatches to the category-registered handler
partB_workerInventory.accessesTenantOrSensitiveData: Indirectly — delegates to whichever handler is registered for the message's category
partB_workerInventory.considerationAndRejection: A single organization-status check here, before every handler call, was considered as the most DRY, maximally-covering fix (it would have automatically covered every current and future queue category with one change). It was deliberately NOT implemented: RecruitmentExportWorkerService (Phase 5.1) already has its own handler-level suspension check that sets a specific business-row status (RecruitmentExportJob.status = CANCELLED with a specific errorMessage) and tells the queue 'complete, do not retry.' A blanket pre-handler check at this shared dispatcher would intercept a suspended organization's message BEFORE the recruitment handler ever runs, meaning RecruitmentExportJob.status would simply stay QUEUED forever (misleading to anyone polling export status) while the underlying queue message silently retried or eventually dead-lettered on its own generic ladder — a real behavior change to an already-shipped, already-tested Phase 5.1 guarantee, not a safe no-op addition. Handler-specific fixes (as done for NOTIFICATION_JOBS via InteractionNotificationOrchestrator) were judged safer and were used instead.
partB_workerInventory.reasonNotFixed: Rejected by design to avoid conflicting with the already-tested Phase 5.1 recruitment export worker semantics — see considerationAndRejection.

partB_workerInventory.accessesTenantOrSensitiveData: Only to DELETE old, already-terminal rows (completed/failed interactions, voice transcripts, notifications, agent/workflow executions past their retention window) — platform-wide, not organization-targeted logic
partB_workerInventory.reasonNotFixed: Reviewed and judged out of scope by design: this worker takes no new action ON BEHALF OF a tenant and has no external side effect — it only deletes stale, already-completed rows, which is harmless (arguably still desirable) regardless of an organization's suspension status.

testInfrastructureNotes.sharedTestDatabaseConcurrencyLimitation: Reconfirmed: the canonical full-suite command already uses --no-file-parallelism, which is necessary because at least one spec (management.e2e.spec.ts, via apps/api/src/test/cleanup.ts's deleteAllOrganizationScopedRows) performs a full blanket wipe of the shared TEST_DATABASE_URL and is not safe to run concurrently with any other file touching that same database. A SEPARATE, narrower issue — the 9 pre-existing failures classified above, mostly afterAll foreign-key-ordering crashes — persists even with --no-file-parallelism, because these specific files' own cleanup code does not account for rows other, unrelated test files may have left behind in the same run. Recommended improvement (not undertaken in this task, as it would be unrelated refactoring across ~8 files): either (a) give every e2e spec file its own fully isolated test database/schema per run (the most robust fix, but a meaningful infrastructure change), or (b) fix each affected file's own afterAll to delete ChannelConnection rows before Plugin rows, matching the FK direction, which is a smaller, mechanical, low-risk change but still touches 8 files outside this task's scope and is better done as its own focused cleanup pass.
